question: what are the prereqs for cmps 147 and is it required for both comp sci and math majors?
answer:
CMPS 147 prerequisites: complete one of MATH 021, MATH 022, MATH 024, MATH 100T, MATH 101, MATH 104, MATH 108, MATH 110, or MATH 121; **or** meet one placement-test score: ACCUPLACER Quantitative Reasoning 258, ACCUPLACER Advanced Algebra and Functions 260, ACT Composite 26, or SAT MATH 580. [3]

It is required for the Computer Science BS. [1] For the Mathematics BS, it is an option—not required by itself—in both the Traditional and Teacher Education tracks: each allows CMPS 130 or CMPS 147. [2]

question: how many credits do you need total to graduate and how many of those are gen eds
answer:
For undergraduate graduation, you need at least 128 credits [3]. The Registrar FAQ also says 128 credits overall and notes program requirements differ [2]; the student-success page says a minimum of 128 graduation credits [9]. At least 48 credits must be completed at Ramapo, including your final 32 in residence [3].

The General Education curriculum should not exceed 41 credits [5]. Students take ten General Education courses [4], but the pages do not state a specific Gen Ed credit total. The exact requirements depend on your program [2]. Review the number of classes and credits with your adviser [2].

Registrar: reg@ramapo.edu, (201) 684-7695, D-224 [2][3].

question: im a sophmore with no major yet, if i declare biology now can i still finish in 4 years? whats the course sequence look like for bio
answer:
The pages can’t confirm whether you personally can finish in four years; that depends on your completed credits and coursework. They advise declaring in sophomore year for a four-year goal, and note that some sequential science majors should be started right away. Declare before completing 64 credits. [4][7] After 64 credits, you are considered a junior and must have a declared major. [8]

For your credit-by-credit assessment, contact the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising): (201) 684-7441 or success@ramapo.edu. [9]

Biology BS (General) recommended plan: it applies to students admitted to the major in 2026–2027, so it may not match your catalog year. [3]
• First Year Fall (18 credits): BIOL 111/111L, CHEM 116/116L, CRWT 102, INTD 101.
• First Year Spring (18): BIOL 113/113L, CHEM 117/117L, MATH 110 or 121 or CMPS 147, Gen Ed; PATH 001.
• Second Year Fall (17): BIOL 221, CHEM 211/211L or 206/206L, MATH 122 or statistics option, Gen Ed; PATH 002.
• Second Year Spring (no total listed): Bio Elective I, BIOL 332/332L, CHEM 213/213L or specified Gen Ed if CHEM 206 was taken, Gen Ed; PATH 003.
• Third Year Fall (14.5): BIOL 356, PHYS 111/118L, Bio Elective II w/lab.
• Third Year Spring (17): Bio Elective III, PHYS 113/119L, two Gen Eds.
• Fourth Year Fall (13.5): Bio Elective 4, BIOL 407/407L, Gen Ed.
• Fourth Year Spring (16): four free electives. Total required: 128 credits. [3]
The Student Success page recommends using Recommended Graduation Plans to plan. [7]

question: what does psyc 101 actually cover
answer:
PSYC 101 Introduction to Psychology is 4 credits and has no published prerequisites. [2] It introduces psychology as a field of study and practice, exploring its history, methods, and scope. Topics include learning, perception, cognition, emotion, motivation, abnormal behavior, psychotherapy, social behavior, personality, development across the lifespan, and the biological bases of thought, feeling, and action. [2]

question: whats the recommended first year sequence for nursing, is it too late to start it as a sophomore
answer:
For the Nursing Generic BSN, the recommended plan is for students admitted in 2025–2026 [2]. First Year, Fall Semester (total 17 credits): INTD 101 - FIRST YEAR SEMINAR (4); CHEM 111 - PRINCIPLES OF CHEMISTRY LECTURE (4); CHEM 111L - PRINCIPLES OF CHEM LAB/RECITAT (1); CRWT 102 - CRITICAL READING AND WRITING II (4); General Education Requirement * (4); PATH TS1 - CAREER PATHWAYS MODULE 1 FOR THEORETICAL & APPLIED SCIENCE [2]. First Year, Spring Semester (total 16 credits): General Education Requirement * (4) twice; PSYC 101 - INTRODUCTION TO PSYCHOLOGY (4); Quantitative Reasoning – MATH 108 - ELEMENTARY PROBABILITY AND STATISTICS (4) [2]. The plan says CRWT placement is CRWT 101 to CRWT 102; CRWT 101S to CRWT 102S, and Math placement is MATH 021/022 to MATH 108-121 [2].

The Generic BSN plan places general education and science requirements in the first two years, then a two-year nursing sequence [2]. The pages don’t establish whether it’s too late for you personally. One advising page says some large, sequentially designed science majors should be started right away [7]. Students with 32 or more completed credits are considered second-year students; declared students are assigned a faculty advisor in their major [8]. Contact the School of Science, Nursing, and Health Office at SNHOffice@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7734, or the Center for Student Success (Academic Advising) at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441 [8].

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BSN-NURG) [7](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/) [8](https://www.ramapo.edu/myadvisor/advisement-by-year/)

question: which major should i pick, environmental science or biology, i like both lol
answer:
I can’t tell you which one you should pick—that depends on your interests, and the pages don’t make that decision for you. [1][2] Biology emphasizes life processes, from molecular to community and evolutionary perspectives, with flexibility to pursue interests. [1] Environmental Science emphasizes multidisciplinary environmental problem-solving; its core includes GIS, sustainable natural resources, environmental chemistry and ecological field research. [2]

To decide, Ramapo suggests: define the decision; gather information by reading the catalog, attending School events, asking questions, and talking with advisors and students; try career-center computer tests; consider the PLACE course, talking with juniors/seniors and professional advisors, and a related summer job; focus on your top choices by taking helpful classes and talking with faculty; consider risks and costs, and get co-op or internship experience before graduating. The page says you should have a pretty clear idea by sophomore year. [3]

The Center for Student Success specializes in helping students choose majors. Contact it at success@ramapo.edu or (201) 684-7441, D-207. [3]

Sources: [1](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-BIOL) [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SN-BS-ENSC) [3](https://www.ramapo.edu/studentsuccess/major/)

question: how many credits is the business minor and do the intro accounting classes count for it if i end up majoring in econ instead
answer:
The Accounting minor is 24 credits [2]. It requires ACCT 221 (Principles of Financial Accounting) and ACCT 222 (Principles of Managerial Accounting) [2]. Both are also required ASB courses for the Economics BA [3], so they can count toward the minor; courses required for your major may overlap with a minor, up to half of the minor’s credits [4].

Sources: [2](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-MN-ACCT) [3](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/programs/SB-BA-ECON) [4](https://catalog.ramapo.edu/pages/R532kjMfIcfnIkM0srb3#integrity-of-degree-programs1)
